desc: A boulder or cliff chunk. Geometrically the safest subject on this path - no thin parts and no back that anyone can check.
source_prompt: a single grey granite boulder, angular fractured faces, chipped edges, broad flat base, the whole boulder inside the frame with margin on all sides, three-quarter view, flat mid-grey seamless background, even frontal light, no cast shadow, no ground plane, no grass, no moss, no other rocks
output: untextured GLB mesh, POSITION attribute only, ~525k tris, ~8.5 MB, 19.5 s
usable_for: terrain scatter base, sculpt base, blockout, 3D-print base, distant prop
not_usable_for: direct game import - needs retopology, UV unwrap and texture bake
note: Best-case subject for single-view 3D and worth knowing why: there are no thin parts for the iso-surface to lose, no interior, and the invented back of a rock is indistinguishable from a real one, so the model's main weakness costs nothing. Also the one preset that survives aggressive decimation - at 5 percent it still reads as the same rock. A rock still needs a UV unwrap before it can take a material that is not flat grey.
